verdicts: The worlds are fair tests: the informed reference dies less than half as often as chance in both worlds at every number of needs, the unit-free arms are bit-identical to the earlier X0.8 code, units differ 10x, and in world U2 rate times unit is constant
REF/RANDOM deaths per 10k at N=6: U1 37.3/234.0, U2 18.3/463.3; parity True
When units differ but the needs are equally urgent (world U1), the raw sum breaks: it has more deaths than the sum with units divided out (6 needs, paired difference above 0)
In that world the weakest-need-first rule, which needs no units, beats the raw sum (6 needs, paired difference below 0)
When the largest unit sits on the slowest need (world U2) the raw sum is hurt more than in U1 (difference of the SUM-minus-SUMN gaps above 0)
In world U2 the fastest need (smallest unit) causes more than 40% of the raw sum's deaths
